reason: This passage (Exodus 15, the Song of Moses) consistently portrays elite figures unfavorably: Pharaoh and his chosen military captains (מִבְחַ֥ר שָׁלִשָׁיו) are drowned in the sea; a boastful enemy warrior claims he will pursue and spoil but is defeated; and the leaders/chiefs (אַלּוּפֵי אֱד֔וֹם, אֵילֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב) of neighboring peoples are depicted as seized with terror and rendered motionless by fear. The only elite presence that receives favorable treatment is implicitly the Israelite leadership (Moses), but the focus is on foreign and opposing elites being destroyed, defeated, or terrified.
